note: Language fallback: the questionnaire was administered to 400 primary and secondary school teachers in Xinjiang, China, and the wording shipped here is the authors' English rendering from the S1 Data column headers. Neither S1 Data nor S2 Data nor the article contains a single CJK character (checked programmatically: 0 across both workbooks' headers and cells), and the paper never states the administration language explicitly, so language=Chinese is an inference from the sample and the questionnaire's title rather than a stated fact. Second caveat: the paper's Results prose quotes several items in a different English rendering than the S1 headers (e.g. header item 5 'I try to lead and effectively interact with individuals from different backgrounds, ethnicities, and cultures simultaneously.' vs prose 'I attempt to guide students from different backgrounds and cultures to interact effectively'); the S1 header wording is shipped because it is the file the IRW table was built from. Third: items 14-16 are phrased in the second person ('You have a very good understanding of teacher leadership.') while items 1-13 are first person; that is how the source file reads and was not normalised. No instructions text is published anywhere in the article or supplements, so instructions is blank.
